bib.title: AutoEnvScaling: Automating the Data Flywheel with Terminal Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AutoEnvScaling: Automating the Data Flywheel with Terminal Agents". First author Simon Yu (Northeastern/Microsoft Research; internship), with Baolin Peng, Bo Liu, Natasha Jaques, Weiyan Shi, Jianfeng Gao and others. Preprint, arXiv:2610.14163v1 [cs.SE], 9 Oct 2026. No venue.

COVERAGE: 44 of 44 pages read (129,270 chars), including appendices A-I and the proposer skills text (E). Pages 29-30 (D.1-D.2 code and workspace listings) were only partly read. References were skimmed. Figures were read through their extracted captions and labels, not by image.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Running environment design as a terminal task (proposer agent in a sandbox) raises the valid-environment rate sharply over prompt-only generation. Bears on note 06.
 number: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 3.5% to 89.0%; Opus 5 74.6 to 94.0; Sol 41.1 to 86.3.
 setup: 8 frontier proposers, 3 methods (Prompt, Prompt+Env Feedback, AutoEnvScaling). "Valid" means the environment builds, the reference solution passes, and an empty solution fails. 95% CIs in Table 2.
 quote: "The largest gain is for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, from 3.5% with Prompt to 89.0% with AutoEnvScaling." (p7)
2. Cost per valid environment falls for 6 of 8 models, by up to 75%. It rises 1.5-1.6x for Opus 5 and GPT-6-astra (Table 2, p7).
 quote: "lowers cost per valid environment for six of the eight models, with reductions of up to 75% compared with Prompt" (p7)
3. Solver gains on held-out Terminal-Bench 2.1 over a matched static Tmax pool. Bears on note 06.
 number: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 34.6 to 38.9 (+4.3, Sol proposer); 35.5 to 39.3 (+3.8, Opus 5). Qwen3.5-9B 27.2 to 33.5 (+6.3) and 29.2 to 36.6 (+7.4). Base scores: 26.7 (35B) and 19.1 (9B).
 setup: avg@5, with CIs of about ±2. RL with group size 16 and 16 prompts per batch, 128k max sequence length, matched solver steps (not matched compute). The Tmax pool was regenerated with the same proposer. Frontier proposers have fixed weights and improve only through their harness. Pi coding agent, 4 CPU / 8 GiB. No seed count is given for RL runs.
 quote: "outperforming the matched Tmax baselines by 4.3 and 3.8 points" (p8)
4. Solver feedback ablation: removing past solver trajectories from the proposer workspace drops Qwen3.5-35B-A3B by 3.6 points (Sol) and 6.7 (Opus 5). That leaves it +0.7 over Tmax with Sol and 2.9 below Tmax with Opus 5 (Table 3, p8).
5. Self-improvement with one model as both proposer and solver (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). Bears on note 06 and note 07, via the proposer reward.
 number: TB2.1 41.1 to 53.3 (+12.2; +6.1 over Tmax). TB4.0 1.6 to 3.2 (Tmax 1.4 gain). Rollout collection 42% faster; usable-group rate 3.1x Tmax. Bears on note 10.
 setup: base model's valid rate is 32.3%, so a Cold-Start SFT on 600 proposer trajectories (from Opus 5, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K3) raises it to 86.8%. DPPO (Qi 2026). Evaluated through 288 solver updates. A single run per condition appears to be shown, with no seeds reported.
 quote: "raises avg@5 from 41.1 to 53.3, a 12.2-point gain and 6.1 points above Tmax" (p9)
6. Proposer training is needed for stability. Without the proposer reward, the valid rate falls to 22.4% by step 160 and training collapses. With proposer training it ends at 94.7%. At step 160, TB2.1 is 48.9 (full), 44.9 (Tmax) and 40.1 (ablation). (G.1-G.2, p40)
7. Execution self-check ablation (Table 11, p39): valid rate rises when the reference solution is run during generation. Opus 5 52.0 to 94.0; Sol 19.5 to 84.8; DeepSeek-V4-Flash 19.4 to 73.0. This run includes solver calibration, so its rates differ from Table 2.
8. Generated environments are richer and harder (Fig 5, p7). Data files per environment: 3.5 for Prompt vs 20.4. Solver turns: 33.8 vs 47.2. Solver pass rate: 61.0 vs 51.0%.
9. HiL-Bench (learning to ask for help, p11): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on held-out software engineering tasks reaches task success 33.9% and Ask-F1 55.3% after cold-start plus RL on 500 generated tasks. Cold-start plus RL on the 100 official tasks gives 6.8% and 29.6%. Opus 5 gets 7.5% task success and 14.4 Ask-F1 in the ask_human setting.
10. Cross-domain generation (App C, p20): 1,061 of 1,489 evaluable runs accepted (71.3%) across 7 domains and 3 coding agents. Acceptance ranges from 100% (terminal) to 26.2% (browser, Opus 5). Only generation and validation were tested; no training was run.

HOW ENVIRONMENTS ARE GENERATED AND VERIFIED (note 06, note 10)
- Each proposer episode produces one Harbor task (instruction, container, reference solution, tests). The proposer works in a sandbox with solver rollouts, past environments, memory and tools, and restricted web access. Benchmark pages are blocked. Admission checks run outside the sandbox.
- Each assignment names a parent environment with the solver's pass rate and most common failure. The proposer builds an easier variant if the solver keeps failing and a harder one if it succeeds.
- Validation: the reference solution must score 1 and an empty solution must score under 0.5. The host also runs a 13-gram contamination check against Terminal-Bench 2.1/4.0 tasks, plus harbor check, a task review by the proposer's own model against the Terminal-Bench rubric (all criteria except binary_reward).
- Calibration (G.4): mean solver reward in [0.25, 0.75] with std at least 0.1. It starts with 4 rollouts and expands to 8 near a band edge. Up to 2 revisions are allowed per assignment. The pool (256 tasks) is re-checked every 16 solver updates.
- Proposer reward (Eq 2, note 07): -1 if validation fails, -0.25 if validation passes but calibration fails, +1 if both pass. Solver reward is the fraction of tests passed (Eq 1). Advantages are mean-centred per role with no std division. Proposer groups hold 128 trajectories. Groups with no reward variance are dropped, DAPO-style.
- The skill text tells the proposer that reward spread is the primary goal ("[0,1] and [0.5,0.5] both average 0.5, but only the first has group-relative learning signal").

BASELINES: Prompt (pipeline synthesis); Prompt+Env Feedback (RST / Environment Evolution style); static Tmax pool (Ivison 2026), regenerated with the same proposer. Ablations: no solver rollouts, no proposer training, no reference self-check.

LIMITS (A.1 and elsewhere)
- Gains over longer training are not established. TB4.0 stays very low (3.2).
- Passing validation does not guarantee correctness. The reference solution and tests share an author, so shared mistakes and shortcut rewards are missed. Reward-hacking exposure is only discussed as future work.
- Cross-domain results show feasibility only, with no downstream training gains.
- Cold-Start gives no detected change in solving (TB2.1 avg@5 40.0 to 41.1; paired change 1.1pp, 95% CI [-4.9, 7.4], p=0.88).
- Comparisons match solver updates, not compute. The harness reports lower absolute scores than model cards (Pi agent, small sandboxes).
- Several proposers and solvers are closed or newly named models. Some Figure 21 comparisons use different assignment suites.
- Proposer quality is judged by the proposer's own model (harbor check).

BUILDS ON: Tmax (Ivison et al. 2026); Harbor (2026) and its create-task skill; Terminal-Bench 2.1/4.0; AutoData (Kulikov 2026); SPADE (Liu 2026); Continual Harness (Karten 2026) for harness updates; DPPO (Qi 2026); DAPO (Yu 2025, cited as [55]); RST; Environment Evolution; SETA; Endless Terminals; unsupervised environment design (Dennis 2020).

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p1) gives all three headline results. Fig 3 (p4) shows the proposer/solver roles and rewards. Fig 4 (p6) shows valid-environment rate by model. Fig 6 (p8) shows the self-improvement curves and the collapse without proposer training. Fig 20 (p41) shows proposer validity over training.

CODE: none beyond the skills. The auto_env_scaling skill text is at pp38-39 and the workspace layout at p30. The Harbor task layout is at pp31-32.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The paper cites model names I do not recognise (GPT-5.6-sol, Claude Opus 5, Qwen3.6, Terminal-Bench 4.0); I report them as printed and have not verified them. Extraction has no spaces in some places (for example "AutoEnvScalingincreases"). Pages 29-30 were not read in full.

QUOTES FOR NOTES
- p2: "treats environment design as a terminal task" (abstract and p2).
- p5: "These checks cannot catch a mistake that the reference solution and the tests share, since the proposer wrote both, nor tests that reward a shortcut."
- p8: "When we keep the weights shared but remove the proposer-side training, the model improves at first and then declines as environment validation errors grow and destabilize training" (this is on p9 of the PDF).
